121NoteKEY REALIZATION: The sensor spec sheet allows, per sensor, up to: slope error 0.03 frac of rise, calibration residual 0.3 C, ambient drift 0.5 C, noise 0.5 sigma + 1.0 quantization. A "gain of -0.05" on core5 EXCEEDS the 0.03 slope bound, so a true gain fault must be beyond -3% of rise. My core5 deficit estimates were -0.7% to -2.5% of rise — INSIDE the spec envelope. Yet my 5 commits that included core5 gain faults (or quadratic core2) all failed. Both signs of error are suspicious. RE-EXAMINE with fresh eyes: maybe the truth is (a) core2 fault form/magnitude wrong, (b) core5 is NOT a fault (within spec) and the real model problem is elsewhere, or (c) both core2 and core5 are model faults. Since model fault magnitudes are reported as model/reality - 1 in the CONDUCTANCE sense, and the self/neighbor asymmetry at core5 pointed to a lateral edge into core5, test whether adjusting one edge in the RC model reproduces the data.
